title: OpenCode HTTP Assistant Completion Reader
summary: The FP-MCP-251 read-only OpenCode HTTP assistant completion reader was verified against an existing live canary session. A fresh tiny assistant-completion probe was first run with cleanup disabled to create session ses_0d5e10bf0fferWGbj7B9Hk8Ec8 and produce assistant output. The new reader then inspected that existing session with expectedText=OPENCODE_HTTP_CANARY_OK. The reader returned readRan=true, completionState=COMPLETED, assistantCompletionObserved=true, expectedTextObservedInAssistant=true, userExpectedTextObserved=true, messagesHttpStatus=200, messagesContentType=application/json, messagesTopLevelType=array, messagesCount=2, assistantMessageCount=1, assistantTextPartCount=1, userTextPartCount=1, assistantTextPaths=["[1].parts[2].text"], userTextPaths=["[0].parts[0].text"], boundedAssistantTextExcerpts=["OPENCODE_HTTP_CANARY_OK"]. The reader confirmed sessionCreated=false, promptSubmitted=false, waitEndpointCalled=false, sessionDeleted=false, runnerStartEndpointContacted=false, and opencodeStarted=false. This verifies the reusable read-only role-aware completion reader against the completion rule admitted in FP-MCP-250.
caveats: A fresh canary session was intentionally created with cleanup disabled so the read-only reader had an existing live session id to inspect.
The session ses_0d5e10bf0fferWGbj7B9Hk8Ec8 remains in OpenCode after this test because the reader is deliberately non-destructive and does not delete sessions.
Both user and assistant messages contained OPENCODE_HTTP_CANARY_OK; completionState=COMPLETED was based on assistant-role text, not user text.
The reader performs a single read of /session/{id}/message and does not poll; polling/orchestration should be implemented by a higher-level runner or future tool.
boundaries: The completion reader did not create a session.
The completion reader did not submit a prompt.
The completion reader did not call any wait endpoint.
The completion reader did not delete the session.
The completion reader did not start OpenCode.
The completion reader did not contact the ForgePilot runner start endpoint.
The completion reader did not create, consume, or authorize execution approval.
The completion reader did not request any file-editing task from the model.
